data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's structural property groups Rule 90 and Rule 184 together as 'number-conserving (or linear/additive in the case of Rule 90)' and contrasts them with Rule 110's 'irreversible non-linear interactions.' This conflation obscures the fact that Rule 184 is NOT additive/linear over GF(2) and Rule 90 is NOT number-conserving. These are two distinct properties unequally distributed across the two rules, so neither property individually separates the passing pair from the failing one. 'Number-conserving OR linear' is a disjunctive ad hoc union of two unrelated mechanisms with no single causal pathway explaining why both rules satisfy the bound. Furthermore, Rule 184 is not reversible (it is many-to-one), so appealing to the absence of 'irreversible' interactions to explain Rule 184's short cycles contradicts Rule 184's actual dynamics.
